title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892–1894 — settlement/accounting and installation/exhibition clocks
research_question: What remains to happen after a Blaschka shipment has physically arrived, and can post-arrival accounting and exhibition handling be reconstructed as distinct transport regimes?
current_thesis: Arrival is not the end of transport. A shipment can continue administratively through broker bills, residual charges and customs release, and physically through unpacking, mounting, exhibition movement and vibration. These processes create settlement and installation clocks independent of the cargo's point-to-point travel time.

analytical_value: A model can arrive at an exhibition in good condition and then become damaged after installation.
Protective mounting material can reverse function: velvet intended to immobilize objects becomes an agent of movement.
Display is another handling/transport regime, not the stable endpoint of freight.
Goodale's repair and stress testing show receiving/exhibition practice actively redesigning object stability.

route_inference_guards: BLA-D00140 directly names 'Ocean and the Sound Steamers' for the March 1893 settled shipment. This is evidence for that shipment only and must not be back-projected onto U.B.346–350 in 1892.
The Sound-steamer carrier and exact New York/Boston transfer point remain unidentified.
Goodale's September 1893 reference to Col. Wales's previous visit proves a residual charge, but does not by itself identify which earlier shipment/inspection generated it.
Do not infer E. A. Snow's first name from initials or unrelated directory entries.

strongest_new_formulations: An invoice can function as a retrospective route map: it reassembles German rail, ocean carriage, Sound-steamer carriage, customs, inspector transport and commission after those movements have occurred.
Transport can remain administratively unfinished after the object has arrived; omitted charges and broker settlement continue on a separate clock.
Installation does not terminate mobility. At Chicago, supposedly stabilized models were remobilized by their display support/environment and required repair plus a new stabilization procedure.

A durable route is partly a durable memory of whom to address, who pays, who brings the inspector and who knows the routine. The Snow chain shows that this memory can persist after the intermediary ceases to exist.
